## Purpose

This procedure describes the general operation, calibration, and
quality control framework for colorimetric water analysis using the
Hach DR3900 benchtop spectrophotometer and the Hach DR900 portable
colorimeter. The SOP is designed as a modular framework: Section 6
covers instrument operation common to all analyses, while the
**Method Registry** (Section 7) provides chemistry-specific parameters
for each analyte (reagent kit, Hach method number, wavelength, range,
reaction time, and interferences). New chemistries can be added to the
registry as the lab's needs evolve, without rewriting the core SOP
[@hach_dr3900; @hach_dr900; @apha2012].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Colorimetric determination of nutrients (phosphorus,
  nitrate, nitrite, ammonia), metals (iron, manganese, copper, zinc,
  lead, chromium), and other water quality parameters (silica,
  sulfate, chloride, hardness) in surface water, groundwater,
  wastewater, and aqueous extracts using Hach pre-packaged reagent
  kits and stored programs
- **Does not apply to:** Analyses requiring external standards and
  user-prepared calibration curves (use the DR3900 in manual wavelength
  mode with a separate SOP); soil KCl extracts analyzed for
  NO~3~^-^/NH~4~^+^ via ion chromatography or flow injection (see
  [SOP-L403](SOP-L403-nitrate-ammonium-kcl.qmd))
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133 (DR3900); field sites
  (DR900)


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve methods, review QC data             |
| Lab Manager       | Maintain instruments, stock reagent kits, track lot numbers and expiration dates |
| Trained Personnel | Run analyses per this SOP, record results   |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## Definitions

- **Absorbance (A):** The negative base-10 logarithm of transmittance:
  $A = -\log_{10}(T)$; directly proportional to analyte concentration
  within the linear range of the instrument (Beer-Lambert law)
  [@hach_dr3900].
- **Beer-Lambert law:** The relationship between absorbance, path
  length, and concentration: $A = \varepsilon c l$, where $\varepsilon$
  is the molar absorptivity, $c$ is concentration, and $l$ is the
  optical path length; the physical basis for all colorimetric
  quantification [@apha2012].
- **Blank (reagent blank):** A sample containing all reagents except
  the analyte; used to zero the instrument and correct for background
  absorbance contributed by the reagent matrix [@apha2012].
- **Continuing calibration verification (CCV):** A known-concentration
  mid-range standard analyzed at regular intervals during a run to
  confirm that factory-programmed calibration curves remain accurate;
  acceptance criterion is ±10% of the stated value [@hach_dr3900].
- **Detection limit (MDL):** The minimum analyte concentration
  reliably distinguished from a blank; method-specific and listed in
  the Method Registry (§7); the blank must read within the MDL of zero
  at the start of each session [@apha2012].
- **DR3900:** The Hach benchtop spectrophotometer; wavelength range
  320--1100 nm; uses stored Hach programs or user-defined methods;
  supports 10 mm square, 1-inch round, and 16 mm round cells
  [@hach_dr3900].
- **DR900:** The Hach portable colorimeter; battery-operated; uses
  the same stored-program approach as the DR3900; limited to a subset
  of Hach methods compatible with the 1-inch round cell format
  [@hach_dr900].
- **Hach method number:** A unique numeric identifier for each Hach
  reagent-kit and instrument-program combination; used to select the
  correct stored program on the DR3900 or DR900 and to ensure that
  the correct reagent is paired with the correct calibration curve
  [@hach_water_analysis2024].
- **Method Registry:** The table in §7 of this SOP listing all
  validated Hach methods in use in the EA Program laboratory, with
  analyte, chemistry, program number, reagent catalog number,
  instrument compatibility, range, sample volume, reaction time, key
  interferences, and validation status.
- **Powder pillow:** A heat-sealed foil packet containing a
  pre-weighed, factory-prepared reagent mixture; added directly to
  the sample to initiate the color-forming reaction; eliminates manual
  reagent preparation and reduces sources of error [@hach_water_analysis2024].
- **RPD (relative percent difference):** |A - B| / ((A + B) / 2) × 100;
  used to assess duplicate precision; acceptable RPD is less than 20%
  for concentrations above 5 × the detection limit [@apha2012].
- **TNT plus vial:** A Hach proprietary pre-dosed reagent vial
  containing all required reagents sealed in glass; used with the
  DR3900 for total-nutrient digestion methods (e.g., total phosphorus,
  total nitrogen) [@hach_water_analysis2024].
- **Zeroing:** The process of inserting a reagent blank into the sample
  cell and pressing Zero to set the baseline absorbance to zero for the
  selected program; required before each analytical batch [@hach_dr3900].


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Hach reagent powder pillows and liquid reagents contain
  a variety of chemicals depending on the method. Some contain acids
  (e.g., sulfuric acid in TNT plus vials), heavy metal indicators
  (e.g., cadmium in older nitrate methods), or oxidizers. Always
  review the SDS for each reagent kit before first use.
- **Thermal:** COD and total nutrient digestions use the DRB200 reactor
  block at 150 °C. Use heat-resistant gloves when handling heated vials.
- **Glassware:** Glass vials can break during handling or if heated
  unevenly. Handle with care; wear safety glasses.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves

### Emergency Procedures

For reagent splashes to skin or eyes, flush with water for at least
15 minutes. Refer to
[SOP-L004 Chemical Spill Response](SOP-L004-chemical-spill-response.qmd)
for spill cleanup. For burns from the reactor block, apply cool running
water and seek first aid.

## Procedure

### Startup and Instrument Check

1. Turn on the DR3900 and allow it to complete its self-check (approximately
   30 seconds).
2. Verify the lamp status indicator shows "Ready."
3. Select the stored program for your analyte by program number (see
   §7, Method Registry) [@hach_dr3900].

### Zeroing

1. Fill a clean sample cell with DI water to the fill line.
2. Wipe the cell exterior with a lint-free cloth. Apply silicone oil for
   1-inch round cells.
3. Insert the cell, close the lid, and press **Zero**. The display must
   read 0.00 (within the method detection limit). If it does not, clean
   the cell and re-zero.

### Sample Analysis

1. Fill a clean cell to the fill line with the water sample.
2. Add the reagent (powder pillow or TNT vial) per the method instructions.
3. Cap, invert, and mix as directed. Start the timer for the required
   reaction time.
4. When the reaction time is complete, wipe the cell exterior (apply
   silicone oil for 1-inch round cells).
5. Insert the cell, close the lid, and press **Read**.
6. Record the result, analyte, program number, sample ID, units, date,
   and time in the lab notebook.
7. Rinse the cell three times with DI water before the next sample.

### Shutdown

1. Remove all samples and reagents from the instrument compartment.
2. Wipe the cell compartment with a lint-free tissue if any liquid is
   present.
3. Log the run in the instrument logbook (date, analyst, analytes run,
   and any instrument issues).
4. Turn off the DR3900 if the session is complete.

### Adding a New Method to the Registry

1. Obtain the Hach procedure document for the method (from the kit box
   or [hach.com](https://www.hach.com/resources/procedures)).
2. Review the SDS for all reagents in the kit.
3. Fill in a new row in the appropriate table above with all required
   fields.
4. Run the method on at least 3 known standard concentrations spanning
   the method range to verify that the instrument's stored program
   produces results within ±10% of the standard value.
5. Run DI water blanks to confirm zero reading.
6. Change the status from *TBD* to **Active** once validation is
   complete.
7. Record the validation data, date, and analyst in the QC log.


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### Every Analytical Session

- **Blank:** Run a DI water blank at the start of each session; must
  read within the method MDL of zero [@apha2012].
- **Standard check:** Run one mid-range Hach standard at the start and
  end of each session; acceptance: ±10% of the stated value
  [@hach_dr3900].
- **Duplicates:** Analyze at least 10% of samples in duplicate;
  acceptable RPD less than 20% above 5 × the detection limit.

### Calibration Verification

The DR3900 and DR900 use factory-programmed calibration curves that do
not require user calibration under normal conditions [@hach_dr3900;
@hach_dr900]. However:

- Run a multi-point verification using Hach-supplied standards at least
  annually or when the instrument is serviced.
- If a standard check deviates by more than 10%, clean the cell,
  re-zero, and re-read. If the problem persists, contact Hach
  technical support.


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                          | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Used powder pillow packets and caps | Standard trash (verify SDS; most are non-hazardous) |
| Cadmium-containing reagent waste    | Hazardous waste; EH&S pickup             |
| Reactor block digestion waste (COD) | Collect in labeled acid waste container  |
| Used sample cells (glass)           | Rinse thoroughly; reuse or recycle       |
| Rinse water (DI)                    | Drain                                    |

## Training Record

Before running analyses on the DR3900 or DR900 independently,
personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and [SOP-L215](SOP-L215-hach-dr3900-spectrophotometer.qmd)
   in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Review the SDS for all reagent kits to be used
4. Observe a trained operator perform startup, blank zeroing, sample
   analysis, and a standard check for at least two analytes
5. Run a full session (blank, standard check, samples, duplicate)
   under supervision with acceptable QC results
6. Add at least one new method to the registry and validate it before
   using it on real samples
7. Be signed off by the lab manager or PI
